title: QUIC RFC 9369 Version 2 Static Floor Architecture
purpose: Describe how the RFC 9369 static version-2 floor is satisfied by the version-aware packet, Initial, and Retry helper surfaces.
design_summary: The QUIC v2 floor is implemented as a version-aware helper layer. `QuicVersionNegotiation` recognizes version 2, maps its long-header packet-type bits, and keeps the version-specific packet-type decisions visible to the parser. `QuicPacketParsing` and `QuicPacketParser` reuse that mapping so version 2 Initial, 0-RTT, Handshake, and Retry packets are classified correctly while the version-1 parser defaults remain intact. `QuicInitialPacketProtection` and `QuicTlsKeySchedule` switch the Initial salt and HKDF labels on the version number so v1 and v2 Initial protection are derived from distinct inputs, and `QuicRetryIntegrity` switches the Retry integrity secret material and packet parsing on the version carried by the Retry packet. The endpoint, runtime, listener, and handshake-flow helpers thread the selected version through their version-aware parse and protection calls so the static v2 wire floor stays explicit in tests. The compatible-version runtime-selection follow-up remains outside this architecture slice.
risks: If a version-agnostic parser default leaks back in, the v2 packet-type mapping can regress silently because the version-specific helpers will still compile.
The v2 Initial and Retry crypto inputs must stay version-bound; reusing the v1 labels or secret material would create an apparently working but incorrect implementation.
The compatible-version runtime-selection flow remains outside this slice and must not be inferred from the static v2 helpers alone.

supplemental_sections.heading: Boundary
supplemental_sections.content: This architecture stays inside the static QUIC v2 floor. It does not add the RFC 9368 compatible-version restart/selection flow or any HTTP/3-specific negotiation behavior.
